id: title:DanielVisca:link backend logs and spans to the frontend session

observations.behavior: Adds authenticated user's distinct_id to logging context and trace span with key posthogDistinctId.
observations.posthog_connection: Supports Logs & Tracing person identity linking; P1.3

observations.behavior: Binds browser session ID from X-Posthog-Session-Id header to structlog and OpenTelemetry span as sessionId.
observations.posthog_connection: Connects frontend sessions for unified identity across app API calls; P1.3

observations.behavior: Tests that team_id and posthogDistinctId are bound only when the request is authenticated, otherwise no bindings occur.
observations.posthog_connection: Validates authentication-dependent behavior and absence of false positives; P1.4}],

observations.limitations: No tests cover concurrent requests or edge cases where multiple middleware modify the same span; tier remains bounded by implementation and test coverage rather than systemic risk reduction.

review.limitations: No tests cover concurrent requests or edge cases where multiple middleware modify the same span; tier remains bounded by implementation and test coverage rather than systemic risk reduction.
review.reason: Changes add two new identity fields (sessionId, posthogDistinctId) to shared middleware, including sanitization and conditional binding based on authentication status, with corresponding unit tests. This supports cross-service identity correlation without changing broader architecture or introducing untested dependencies. No evidence of wider adoption or incident prevention; score capped at 2.
review.posthog_relevance: Adds missing identity context required for Logs & Tracing person links and correlates browser sessions with backend identities, supporting debugging and attribution workflows.
review.uncertainty: Could not assess production impact or compatibility with existing tracing setups; could not distinguish whether this change resolves a latent issue or merely fills gaps in identity propagation.
